etymologies.etymologyHTML: From economic +‎ -al.

definitions.definition: Careful with money so as not to spend too much; prudent; thrifty.

quote.citation: 1961 March, “The new Glasgow Central signalbox”, in Trains Illustrated, page 177:
quote.text: The whole [resignalling] scheme has proved more economical than the construction of a new Clyde bridge.

definitions.definition: (dated) Relating to economy in any other sense.

quote.citation: 1854, Patrick Edward Dove, The Elements of Political Science‎[1], part 2, page 246:
quote.text: In economical science, value and the power of producing value are taken into consideration.

quote.citation: 1922, Eugen von Böhm-Bawerk, Capital and Interest: A Critical History of Economical Theory‎[2], page 218:
quote.text: By Use, then, in the sense given it by the Say-Hermann school, we have to think of an objective useful element which proceeds from goods, and acquires independent economical existence as well as independent economical value.

quote.citation: 2007, Who's Who in the Arab World‎[3], page 312:
2010, New Techniques and Technologies in Mining‎[4], page 20:
quote.text: Economical function usually has anti-crisis orientation and forms stable economical development of the state.
